newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks shatter more records, Nasdaq joins in.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks shatter more records, Nasdaq joins in.

text.p: U.S. stocks shattered more records as investors bet interest rates would remain low and lure fresh funds to equities, but volume was thinned by the absence of some players on the Veteran's Day holiday.

"When you have a market like this, it's like a train leaving the station and everybody wants to get on board...But we're not at the advanced stages of speculation where investors are becoming giddy," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
The Dow industrials surged 36 to about 6256.

It was the Dow's fourth consecutive record closing high and the longest string of records since the seven-session streak from February 5-13. It followed last week's 198-point Election rally -- the second biggest weekly point gain ever.
The S&P 500 rose one to about 732, its fifth consecutive all-time high finish. Likewise, the NYSE Composite rose one to about 387.

The tech-studded Nasdaq Composite rose five to about 1263, topping October 15's record 1258.10. Chip stocks rallied ahead of the Semiconductor Industry Association's book-to-bill report for October, due after the closing bell.
Winners beat losers 13-9 on moderate NYSE volume of about 354 million shares, slowed by the U.S. bank holiday.
The bond market was closed for Veteran's Day. On Friday, the long bond ended down 10/32 to yield 6.51 percent.
Stocks were bolstered by an increasing confidence by more investors the Federal Reserve will hold U.S. monetary policy steady at Wednesday's FOMC meeting.

Equities also got a shot in the arm after Smith Barney raised the stock portion in its recommended asset allocation to 50 percent from 45 percent, cut cash to 10 percent from 15 percent and kept bonds at 40 percent.

Marshall Acuff said the investment policy committee's move was based on a stronger bond market, expectations interest rates would not rise near term and the belief that overseas growth is expanding slowly enough not to pressure U.S. rates.

"We recognize the equity market has done well since July. But typically stocks don't go down in a positive monetary environment. On the other side of the coin, valuations are still high and overall profit growth is projected to slow over time. We're not suggesting everything is right with the world, but typically bull markets end when the Fed tightens and we don't see that anytime soon," the portfolio strategist said.

Meanwhile, flows into stock mutual funds jumped to $2.22 billion for the three-day period ended November 7, compared with $443 million for the two days ended November 4, according to Mutual Fund Trim Tabs.

Chip stocks surged in anticipation that the closely watched book-to-bill ratio may top the 1.0 level for the first time this year. A book to bill of 1.0 means that for every dollar of computer chips shipped, one dollar of new orders was recorded.
Intel was up 1-5/8 to 123-7/8, Micron rose 1-7/8 to 31-7/8 and Atmel added two to 30-7/8.
Among special situations, PHH Corp jumped 17 to 47-3/4 after agreeing to merge with HFS Inc in a $1.7 billion deal that values PHH at $49.50 a share. HFS lost 1-1/4 to 72-7/8.

Drug wholesaler Bergen Brunswig slumped 5-1/8 to 27-5/8 after agreeing to merge with generic drug maker IVAX in a tax-free stock deal valued at $1.65 billion. IVAX fell 3-3/8 to 12-3/8. Arbitragers said Bergen's relationships with other distributors may be impaired and it is making a major strategy shift with a company that is going through some problems.
Dow component Philip Morris rose 1-1/2 to 99-3/8.
The College Retirement Equities Fund said its participants rejected a resolution urging the divestment of its tobacco-related holdings.

Globalstar Telecommunications rose 2-7/8 to 56-1/2 in U.S. trading after reaching an accord with a unit of China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications to extend its planned global mobile satellite system to customers in China.

Globalstar, based in San Jose, Calif, was founded by Loral, up 7/8 to 17-1/2, and QualComm, 2-1/4 to 44-3/4. It also includes France's Telecom, Hyundai, Alcatel Alsthom and Daimler-Benz AAerospace, among others.
Eastman Kodak rose 1-5/8 to 82-5/8. CS First Boston named the stock its featured stock of the week.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 5.16 to 1262.67, a record.
The S&P 500 index rose 1.05 to 731.87, a record.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721.
